system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: How much of the zero-shot localisation quality of MVFA (pixel AUROC and Dice on a held-out modality) is retained when its segmentation adapters are trained without pixel masks, using pseudo-masks drawn only from labelled abnormal source images (a patch is anomalous when its frozen CLIP level-4 feature is farther from every normal patch of the same dataset than the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal nearest-neighbour distances on source validation data), as masks are removed from zero, one, or all three masked source datasets?

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: DINOv2-propagated pseudo-masks tuned on synthetic lesions and mixed with exact synthetic masks
SUMMARY: Propagate label-restricted seeds over DINOv2 affinities, tune the propagation on synthetic lesions with known masks, and train MVFA on a mixture of propagated real pseudo-masks and exact synthetic masks.
HYPOTHESIS: Tuning the DINOv2 propagation length and threshold on synthetic lesions inserted into source normal images selects settings whose pseudo-mask Dice on real lesions is within 3 points of the oracle setting, and a 25% synthetic / 75% propagated-real mixture recovers at least 92% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities.
RATIONALE: DINOv2 propagation turns fragmented CLIP seeds into coherent regions but has two free parameters (walk length T, threshold) that must be chosen without masks, while synthetic lesions have exact masks but unrealistic appearance. The combination keeps each parent's strength and removes its weakness: synthetic lesions provide a label-free way to tune the propagation (insert a lesion into a normal source image, run seed detection and propagation, compare to its known mask), and they also contribute a minority of exactly masked samples to training. Spatial-FAD's evidence on DINO boundary adherence and Fed-LoRA's evidence that tailored synthetic abnormal data help few-shot detection support both parts.
METHOD: 1) Seeds: label-restricted CLIP rule. 2) Propagation: DINOv2 ViT-B/14 (torch.hub) patch affinities (8-neighbours + 10 feature NNs, tau 0.1), s_T = A^T s_0. 3) Tuning: for each source dataset, insert 200 synthetic lesions (Poisson-blended texture from pseudo-anomalous regions of abnormal images, area 0.5-8%) into normal source-validation images, run steps 1-2, and choose T in {1,3,5} and threshold in {0.3,0.5,0.7} x max(s_T) maximising Dice against the synthetic masks. 4) Training set for seg branch: real abnormal images with propagated masks (75%) and synthetic lesions in normal train images with exact masks (25%); normal images as in MVFA. 5) train_zero.py with Focal + Dice unchanged. Hyper-parameters as MVFA.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; seed-only; propagated with synthetic tuning; propagated with oracle tuning on source true masks (upper reference); mixtures rho in {0, 0.25, 0.5}. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice on real lesions (masked sources), trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if synthetic tuning selects settings more than 3 Dice points worse than the oracle or the best mixture recovers less than 85% of the mask-supervised gain.

Idea B:
TITLE: Bounded prototype pseudo-masks with an ignore band for mask-free MVFA segmentation
SUMMARY: Derive pseudo-masks from distances to per-image re-centred normal prototypes, train the segmentation adapters only on confident patches with a sigmoid loss, and measure how much mask-supervised localisation is recovered.
HYPOTHESIS: Training MVFA's segmentation adapters on bounded-prototype pseudo-masks with an ignore band recovers at least 85% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC gain over frozen CLIP on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC, and at least 5 points more pseudo-mask IoU than the static-bank rule of the problem statement.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: supervision of seg_adapters (true masks vs. pseudo-masks, with or without per-image re-centring and ignore band) and the number of masked source datasets whose masks are removed (0, 1, 3). For each source dataset, 32 normal prototypes per level are obtained by k-means on frozen CLIP level-4 patch features of its normal training images. For an abnormal training image, each prototype is re-centred toward the image's own mean patch feature by a bounded step (gate g = 0.2, step norm clipped to 0.5 x the prototype's within-cluster radius). A patch's distance d is its minimum distance to the re-centred prototypes; patches with d above the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal distances (source validation) are labelled anomalous, below the 95th percentile normal, and those in between are ignored. Dependent variables: pixel AUROC and Dice on held-out masked modalities, pseudo-mask IoU against true masks, and image AUROC.
RATIONALE: Pseudo-masks defined against a dataset-wide normal bank (the problem's rule) mark anatomically unusual but healthy patches as anomalous. ReCAP shows that a per-image, bounded re-centring of the normal reference fixes static-anchor errors, and MadCLIP shows that a sigmoid loss handles many-to-one supervision. Combining them gives pseudo-masks with a per-image normal reference and an explicit ignore band for uncertain patches, so the segmentation adapters are only trained where the pseudo-label is confident.
METHOD: 1) New script make_pseudo_masks.py: for each source dataset, extract frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 layer-24 patch features (17x17 grid at 240 px) of normal train images; run k-means (k=32, 5 restarts) to get prototypes P_k and radii r_k (mean distance of members). 2) For each abnormal train image: m = mean patch feature; P_k' = P_k + clip(0.2 (m - P_k), max_norm = 0.5 r_k). Patch distance d_p = min_k ||f_p - P_k'||_2. 3) Thresholds t_lo, t_hi = 95th/99th percentiles of d over normal source-validation images (computed the same way). Label y_p = 1 if d_p > t_hi, 0 if d_p < t_lo, ignore otherwise; upsample to 240x240 with nearest neighbour; save as .npy masks plus an ignore mask. Normal images get all-zero masks. 4) dataset/medical_zero.py: load pseudo-masks and ignore masks for datasets flagged pseudo; seg_idx >= 0 for all six datasets. 5) train_zero.py: replace Focal + Dice on seg_adapters by a masked sigmoid (SigLIP-style) loss L = mean over non-ignored pixels of softplus(-(2y-1)(t s_p + b)), t, b learnable (init 10, -10), plus Dice on non-ignored pixels; det branch unchanged. 6) Model selection by source-validation pixel AUROC computed against pseudo-masks (no target labels). 7) Hyper-parameters: lr 1e-3 (as in the paper), 50 epochs, batch 16 via gradient accumulation, k=32, g=0.2, percentiles 95/99.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on the masked targets BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Checkpoints and all thresholds selected on source-modality validation splits only; MVFA re-run under the same rule as the mask-supervised reference; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: (a) true masks on 3 sources (reference), (b) pseudo-masks replace masks on 1 source, (c) on all 3 sources, (d) (c) plus the image-only datasets as pseudo-mask sources. Ablations: static bank rule (problem statement) vs re-centred prototypes; with vs without ignore band. Metrics: pixel AUROC, Dice at the source-validation-selected threshold, image AUROC, pseudo-mask IoU vs true masks on the three masked datasets. Falsified if condition (c) recovers less than 70% of the gain of (a) over frozen CLIP, or if re-centring does not improve pseudo-mask IoU.
